instructions: Apply the bundled private Commerce schema and deploy the cms-commerce Edge Function.
Install the generated bearer token in the CMS secret store and Supabase function secrets.
Review marketplace settings, offer conditions, workflows, and metadata definitions.
scopes: Marketplace seller registration and offer management
Authenticated buyer carts and seller-grouped checkout
Versioned buyer legal requirements and immutable acceptance evidence
Built-in buyer notifications with optional Emailer delivery
External or disabled notification delivery modes
Commerce settings, workflows, conditions, and metadata
checks: The Commerce schema stays private to anon and authenticated Supabase roles.
Seller and buyer identities come from the CMS-computed x-cms-user-id header.
Cart mutations use optimistic versions, and checkout revalidates every offer before creating seller-grouped orders.
Prices, snapshots, workflow transitions, and ownership are validated by transactional database commands.
Required buyer legal documents are resolved from published CMS pages and accepted before protected payment preparation.
Payment and delivery remain separate integrations linked through immutable order public ids.
resources: Products, catalogue taxonomy, offers, orders, sellers, settings, workflow, and metadata dashboards
Generated private CMS Commerce API key
Private commerce schema, native notification queue, and modular cms-commerce Edge Function
review: Keep publication status separate from configurable workflow state.
Keep price ranges, access rules, and seller verification out of custom metadata.
Do not trust client-provided seller ids, buyer ids, prices, cart projections, order totals, or snapshots.
Do not trust client-provided legal hashes, page content, actors, or acceptance timestamps.
Use metadata only for validated descriptive information.
Keep notification delivery behind the Commerce source contract; never write into a provider database.
sync: Install Commerce source and custom-field overlays
syncNote: Commerce keeps domain state and notification intent in one transactional schema; the configured sender owns message delivery.
